name: MN-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans about 11 points Democratic and the seat is already held by Democrats
Kelly Morrison holds a massive fundraising edge; Tyler Bass reports no fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent
No independent polling of the race; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 11-point Democratic lean, Morrison's incumbency, and her roughly $1.8 million war chest against a challenger with no reported finances all point the same direction, and markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent, consistent with a Safe D hold.
model.watch: Any polling showing a far closer race, late outside spending on Bass's behalf, or a sharp national swing toward Republicans would narrow the outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's 3rd District leans about 11 points toward Democrats, and incumbent Kelly Morrison is running for re-election. She has raised nearly $1.8 million with roughly $555,000 on hand, while Republican challenger Tyler Bass shows no reported fundraising. No independent public polls of the general election are available, and no expert raters currently list the race, so the outlook rests on structural indicators.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent. A solidly Democratic-leaning seat, an incumbent with a large financial advantage, and an opponent with no visible campaign resources all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with an expected margin in the low 20s and only a small chance of an upset.
